title: Introducing Trace Queries
summary: Find slow or failed runs for your coding agent to fix.
body_markdown:
You can now use[trace queries](https://mastra.ai/reference/observability/tracing/trace-query) to filter and find traces that match specific criteria. Mastra platform and Studio support trace filtering by time range, primitive type, environment, status, score, feedback, and more. Your coding agent can run the same queries, then fix what it finds.


Trace queries usually match fields on the trace itself: when it ran, which agent ran it, and whether it succeeded. The detail that explains a problem often sits deeper, in a failed tool call, a low score, or thumbs-down feedback. Trace queries can reach low-level information nested deep within a trace to provide a more detailed view of what really happened.


Your browser does not support the video tag.


Each query can combine up to 100 conditions, using fields like` entityName` ,` environment` ,` spans.model` ,` scores.score` , and` feedback.value` , with up to 8 filters on trace internals (` spans` ,` scores` , or` feedback` ) rather than fields on the trace itself. A query's` timeRange` can cover any of your retained trace data, as long as` from` is earlier than` to` ; the 31-day maximum was[removed in @mastra/core 1.78.0](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/27042) .


Trace queries work on Mastra platform and on self-hosted Mastra projects where` storage.observability` uses DuckDB, PostgreSQL, or ClickHouse. If your trace data lives outside of Mastra, you can bring your existing history over with[trace imports](https://mastra.ai/blog/introducing-trace-imports-for-mastra-platform) .


## Get started


Trace queries need a platform access token and your project ID, sent with each request. Use the correct Mastra observability[base URL](https://mastra.ai/docs/mastra-platform/api) for your project's region:


- **US** :` https://observability.mastra.ai`
- **EU** :` https://observability.eu.mastra.ai`


There are four ways to run queries: Mastra CLI, Mastra platform and Studio, Mastra Client SDK, and observability endpoints. Each code example below finds agent traces from the last 7 days that ended in an error.


### Mastra CLI


Install or upgrade the Mastra CLI globally:


Terminal


```text
npm   install   -g   mastra@latest
```


note


Requires` mastra@1.30.0` or later, added in[PR #23680](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/23680) .


Run the[mastra api trace query](https://mastra.ai/reference/cli/mastra#mastra-api-trace-query) command from your terminal. The CLI reads` MASTRA_PLATFORM_ACCESS_TOKEN` and` MASTRA_PROJECT_ID` from your environment:


Terminal


```text
mastra   api   --url   https://observability.mastra.ai   trace   query   '  {
"timeRange": { "from": "2026-10-07T00:00:00.000Z", "to": "2026-10-14T00:00:00.000Z" },
"where": {
"op": "and",
"args": [
{ "op": "eq", "left": { "path": "entityType" }, "right": { "literal": "agent" } },
{ "op": "eq", "left": { "path": "status" }, "right": { "literal": "error" } }
]
}
}  '
```


### Mastra platform and Studio


On Mastra platform and Studio, the **Traces** tab lets you filter by time range, primitive type, environment, status, score, feedback, and more.


### Mastra Client SDK


Use[queryTraces()](https://mastra.ai/reference/observability/tracing/trace-query#query-traces-with-the-client-sdk) with` MastraClient` :


Terminal


```text
npm   install   @mastra/client-js@latest
```


note


Requires` @mastra/client-js@1.44.0` or later, added in[PR #22728](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/22728) .


src/traces.ts


```text
import   {   MastraClient   }   from   "  @mastra/client-js  "  ;


const   mastraClient   =   new   MastraClient  ({
baseUrl:   "  https://observability.mastra.ai  "  ,
headers: {
Authorization:   `  Bearer   ${  process.env.MASTRA_PLATFORM_ACCESS_TOKEN  }`  ,
"  X-Mastra-Project-Id  "  : process.env.MASTRA_PROJECT_ID  !
}
});


const   {   traces   }   =   await   mastraClient.  queryTraces  ({
timeRange: {
from:   "  2026-10-07T00:00:00.000Z  "  ,
to:   "  2026-10-14T00:00:00.000Z  "
},
where: {
op:   "  and  "  ,
args: [
{ op:   "  eq  "  , left: { path:   "  entityType  "   }, right: { literal:   "  agent  "   } },
{ op:   "  eq  "  , left: { path:   "  status  "   }, right: { literal:   "  error  "   } }
]
}
});
```


### Observability endpoints


You can also send a` POST` request using the[trace query endpoint](https://mastra.ai/reference/observability/tracing/trace-query#send-an-http-request) . The request includes` MASTRA_PLATFORM_ACCESS_TOKEN` and` MASTRA_PROJECT_ID` variables in the headers:


For more information and full configuration options, see:


- [Advanced trace queries reference](https://mastra.ai/reference/observability/tracing/trace-query)
- [Client SDK observability reference](https://mastra.ai/reference/client-js/observability)
- [mastra api trace query CLI reference](https://mastra.ai/reference/cli/mastra#mastra-api-trace-query)
